newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Piltel lowers 1996 profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Piltel lowers 1996 profit forecast.

text.p: Shares in cellular phone operator Pilipino Telephone Corp fell to a year low on Monday after the firm said earnings in the first nine months were affected by losses from fraudulent calls.

Piltel said at the start of trading that its net income in the first nine months of the year grew by 27 percent to 722.4 million pesos ($27.57 million) from 568.2 million in the same period last year.
The company also announced it was cutting its profit forecast for the full year.

"The revenue and profit figures would have been much higher had it not been for sizeable opportunity losses due to technical problems which congested the network of Mobiline, the firm's cellular service," Piltel chief financial officer Ignatius Yenko said in a statement.
"With aggregate opportunity losses due to illegal calls estimated at 300 million pesos by year-end, the company is reducing its end 1996 net income forecast by 10 percent," Yenko said.
Piltel, a unit of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co PS, had earlier forecast a 1996 full year net income of 1.16 billion pesos.

The firm's acknowledgement of problems due to fraudulent calls sent its shares to a year-low of 20.75 pesos at midsession on foreign selling before rebounding to 23 pesos at the close, from 24 pesos on Friday.
Piltel has fallen by 35.2 percent since the start of month, from its close of 35.50 pesos on October 1.
"Investors have been selling down the issue since the start of the month on rumours of weak earnings this year," said one broker.
"I am now thinking of downgrading Piltel's net income this year to 969 million pesos from my earlier estimate of 1.389 billion pesos," said Alexis Cabel, analyst at Angping Securities.

Brokers said Piltel had to convince investors that it could protect itself from cloning, which occurs when people copy encoded data to enable calls to be made free of charge from another mobile phone.
"What Piltel's anti-cloning device will do will be crucial not only to Piltel but the industry as a whole," Cabel said.

Piltel also told the Philippine Stock Exchange it had made provision for doubtful accounts totalling 105.6 million pesos in the first nine months of the year as against 54.3 million pesos for the same period last year.
The cellular phone industry, which is still in its infancy in the Philippines, is going through a period of growing pains, traders said.
In August, Globe Telecom, the joint venture between Ayala Land Inc and Singapore Telecom, said it lost 505 million pesos in the first six months of the year due to doubtful accounts.
